row.why: She asked about the last ONE meeting (امتى كان آخر واحد؟); he used the plural اجتماعاتي; Amal: 'It's one. اجتماع.' and he took it at 04:12 ('Oh, 'cause it's the last meeting. You're right'). The plural is a separate piece from A3 (aa5er placement) and A4 (gender).

rulings.why: 04:22-04:30 is him searching (الآخر، أخيرة، الأخير، الأخيرة - S5); her 'No. [laughs]' at 04:27 is not tied to one piece, and the same phrase is fixed at 04:37 ('اجتماع is masculine'), which is agreed row A4 (right اجتماعي الأخير). The plural part is D2. Same moment, not its own slip.
No voiced signal; her chat 7awaali alone is not a correction (GR-19). أول (awal) is a near-sound of حوالي with the ح dropped (7awaali -> awaali): most likely the engine or S4, not a wrong word.

row.why: A number said alone (65 degrees, no counted noun after it) keeps the -e: 5amse u sitteen. Amal 'No' (08:10) and 'مش خمس' (08:13); at 06:35 she had just asked when the أ/-e is dropped and he said 'when we're counting'. This is a new slip 2 minutes after A6, not a repeat.

He meant 65 (chat 5amse u sitteen) and the engine wrote ستة عشر (sixteen) for sixty. Her voiced 'No / مش خمس' was before and aimed at خمس (D5); 'Wow' is not a fix, so it goes in as B (let pass). Low: 'sitteen' sounds like English 'sixteen', so the engine may have turned a right ستين into ستة عشر.

He repeated her example الدروس صعبة 5 s later with a different word; in a lesson about feminine adjectives for non-human plurals, السبع is the engine's spelling of el-sa3b (masculine, with el-), not 'the seven'. Amal 'No. صعبة.' and he answered 'Oh, you're saying the singular feminine' - he took her fix. Speaking (him saying the rule's form), not a listening misread.

rulings.why: Duplicate of A9: the same word (zaigish 23:02 -> zaish 23:09 -> 'but zaish' 23:15), one continuous attempt, 13 s after her fix; A9's right تنزعجش already holds the missing n. Her 'بنزعج، صح' says 'right', so the line itself is not clearly wrong.

rulings.why: Amal: 'Fi or fiyo. You could say fiyo. Adi.' - she says both are fine (3adi) and offers fiyo as an option. Brief: Amal saying his version is also valid is not a slip.

row.medi_said: Oh yeah, fio. Matenbisti fio ziyad.
row.proposed_rule: Negating a verb in spoken Levantine adds -ish at the end as well as ma in front: ma tenbestish fiyyo (don't enjoy it), ma tenze3jesh.
row.why: 8 s after her 25:46 'Where's your ish?' (A11) he again said Matenbisti with no -sh, and she asked again 'Where's your ish?'; he answered 'you want me to do ish for all of them?'. Wrong form again after her fix, fixed again = its own slip (GR-32). No bucket covers the -ish ending (B11 is only ma + you-form), so PROPOSE, same as A11.

rulings.why: His 28:35 try already had the right form (in basatetish, with the t); 28:41 'in basata, in basatish' is him wavering (S5), and her 'Inbastatish' matches his first try. At 28:47 he said 'There's two T's, right?' again on his own. Self-fix before help / searching, not a slip.

'So like, for باد I can use like بادات' is a QUESTION about the rule she was explaining (feminine for non-human plurals), not a use in a sentence. Brief: a question about the rule is neither a slip nor a use.
